# How to Use ChatGPT's Memory Feature to Stop Repeating Yourself

Have you ever felt tired of telling ChatGPT the same background information every time you start a new conversation? Whether it is your job title, your dietary requirements, or the fact that you write in Australian English, repeating yourself can feel like a chore. 

Fortunately, you can use the built-in memory feature to make your digital assistant remember your preferences automatically.

## How AI memory works

To solve the problem of constant repetition, ChatGPT has a built-in memory. Think of this memory as a digital notepad where the AI scribbles down important details about you so you do not have to keep re-typing them in future conversations.

When you chat, the AI will automatically identify facts it thinks are useful for the future. Alternatively, you can directly command it to remember something. For example, you can type: "Remember that I write for a local audience." 

The AI will store this in its memory profile (the dedicated setting where it keeps track of your ongoing preferences) and apply it to all your future chats.

## Managing what the AI remembers

Because the AI learns continuously from your conversations, it might occasionally remember something you would rather it forget. Fortunately, managing these details is incredibly simple:

* **To view or delete memories**: Go to your settings menu, select the personalisation option (the menu where you customise how the AI behaves), and click on "Manage Memory". Here, you will see a list of everything the AI knows about you, with clear options to delete individual facts.
* **To edit on the fly**: You can simply tell the AI during a normal chat: "Forget what I just said about my job," or "Update my location to Brisbane."
* **To turn it off entirely**: If you prefer a blank slate every time you open a new window, you can toggle the memory feature completely off in your personalisation settings.

## Smart ways to use memory today

Here are a few practical details you can teach your assistant right now to save time:

* **Your writing style**: Tell it to always use Australian English spelling (such as "colour" and "organisation") and a warm, professional tone.
* **Your household details**: Share your family's dietary restrictions or your pet's name so it can suggest relevant recipes or care tips instantly.
* **Your business context**: Let it know what industry you work in, your professional role, and who your primary customers are.

## What this means for you

* **In everyday life**: You can plan weekly meals, draft letters, or get holiday recommendations that actually match your taste, all without explaining your lifestyle from scratch every single time.
* **For your business or work**: You can maintain a consistent brand voice. Once the AI remembers your target audience and company tone, every email or social media caption it helps you draft will align with your professional standards.
* **If you're just getting started**: Open your chat today and type this simple prompt (the instruction you give to the AI): *"Remember that I prefer clear, concise explanations with no corporate jargon."*

## Wrap-up

With a shared memory, your digital assistant becomes truly personal, saving you valuable time and effort. Take a quick moment today to open your chat settings, ensure the memory toggle is switched on, and give the AI two or three key details about your daily routine to get started.
